events.description:
The 17th Sunday after Pentecost; Sunday Worship with Holy Communion.

College Chaplain Matthew Marohl will deliver the sermon; presided by Associate College Chaplain Sarah Semmler Smith ’04  and assisted by Jonathan Madden ’20, Interim Cantor for the Student Congregation. The Chapel Choir will be conducted by Joseph Kemper ’11, Assistant Professor of Music. Founded in 1925, the St. Olaf Chapel Choir began as one of two mixed choruses at St. Olaf College following the dissolution of the Choral Union. Specializing in the performance of oratorio and larger works, the St. Olaf Chapel Choir frequently collaborates with the St. Olaf Orchestra as well as instrumentalists and soloists from the St. Olaf community.

Sunday Worship is a time of inspiration and worship for body, mind, and spirit; a meaningful beginning to a new week. All are welcome!

Click the web link below to access streamed and archived services.
events.title: Sunday Morning Worship: 17th Sunday after Pentecost

events.description: Crafting Resilience: Finding Community and Connection through Fiber Arts is an artist-led workshop where participants gather together — without technology — to build community while working on a fiber craft of their choosing. Bring your own project that’s in process or start a new one with materials and tools provided; we’ll be working primarily in knitting, crochet, needle-felting, and embroidery. Stop by or stay for the whole time: we’ll get to know each other and share ways that we’re practicing resilience together and on our own. From novice to expert, everyone is welcome and demonstrations will be available for those looking to learn. Light snacks and refreshments provided. This workshop is led by artist and Collections Manager Krista Anderson-Larson and made possible by funding from the Gimse Striving for Peace on Horizon’s Brim Art Endowment.
events.title: Crafting Resilience: Finding Community and Connection through Fiber Arts

events.description:
Faculty, staff, students, and the wider community are welcome to spend an immersive afternoon exploring what it really means to train the voice like an athlete. Through lecture, interactive workshop, and live masterclass, Marci Rosenberg connects exercise physiology, vocal workload and recovery, vocal health, and the science and application of SOVT. Learn practical strategies for building vocal capacity, identifying emerging problems early, managing fatigue and risk, and making smarter training choices in the studio and onstage.

Lecture/Workshop 10 a.m.- 12 p.m. | Masterclass 1 p.m. – 2:15 p.m.

This event is free and open to the public.
events.title: Pedagogy Saturday: The Vocal Athlete Lab
